A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-based RF propagation work, renamed from RFSPM to GSRF, with substantial shared architecture and RFID/BLE experiments. All pages support comparison, including v2's Appendices A-G. V1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original RFID spectrum, BLE RSSI/localization, and LoRa orchard/coverage evaluations in Section 7.

after.justification: V2 reports original RFID, BLE, and complex-CSI evaluations, plus component ablations and parameter studies in Section 5 and Appendices F-G.

M1.justification: V1 models each Gaussian's emission using a two-layer MLP; v2 replaces this with learned complex Fourier-Legendre coefficients. V2 also adds Fourier loss for antenna arrays and replaces averaged amplitude/phase L1 losses with complex squared L2 loss for complex-valued single-antenna signals.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual uplink-to-downlink complex-CSI evaluation on the Argos dataset (Section 5.2), whereas v1 only mentions 5G applications. It removes v1's LoRa orchard RSSI and gateway-coverage experiments (Section 7.3), which are absent from v2's appendices. RFID and BLE/localization coverage remains.

E2.justification: WRF-GS is newly evaluated in RFID quantitative comparisons and BLE prediction/localization comparisons (Appendix F.2, Table 3). The new CSI comparison includes R2F2 and FIRE alongside NeRF2. The FLog comparison disappears with the LoRa study. RF-3DGS and WRF-GS+ are discussed but are not reported as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a CSI protocol using 100,000 measurements, a 70/30 split, 26 uplink and 26 downlink subcarriers, and 30% of the training portion for GSRF versus the full training portion for baselines. It also adds controlled component and parameter experiments. For retained RFID timing comparisons, the reported hardware changes from RTX 3080 Ti or 4090 to RTX 3080 Ti.

E4.justification: V1 contains measurement-density analysis but no component ablations. V2 adds FLE-versus-SH, phase-removal, and Fourier-loss ablations (Table 1), SSIM removal (Appendix G), FLE-degree and angular-resolution sweeps (Tables 4-5), and random-versus-uniform initialization timing (Appendix F.3).

E5.justification: V2 introduces ± reporting for BLE errors and density MSE without defining its statistical meaning. It relabels the RFID 21.2%/56.4% improvements from averages to medians. V1's explicit ten-run RFID timing specification is absent; v2 specifies ten runs for newly reported BLE timings. This does not establish increased replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds CSI results, including 20.99 dB mean SNR, WRF-GS comparisons, BLE timing, and ablation/sensitivity results, while removing LoRa outcomes. It also revises the reported density-summary MSE from 0.0312 for RFSPM (v1 Section 7.1.4) to 0.002147 for GSRF (v2 Appendix F.4). These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains; several headline RFID/BLE numbers remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds FLE radiance definitions, a continuous-to-discrete complex rendering derivation (Appendix A), and explicit ray-intersection and gradient derivations (Appendix D), extending v1's formulas and verbal backward-kernel description. The new mathematics contains inconsistencies: the three-sigma ellipsoid boundary is set to 3 in Appendix A.2 and 9 in Appendix D.3.1.

C1.justification: V2 makes MLP-free FLE radiance and Fourier-domain supervision central innovations. V1 instead foregrounds Gaussian representation with per-Gaussian MLPs, prior-free gradient-guided initialization, and customized ray tracing. The overarching claim of high-fidelity RF synthesis with improved data, training, and inference efficiency remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of FLE versus SH, projection tradeoffs, indirect multipath validation, and antenna-beam applicability, explicitly noting that directional beam data were not tested (Appendix G). Zero-shot and static-scene limitations already existed in v1; v2 expands proposed adaptations but removes the explicit multiple-receiver discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, FLE configuration, a three-dimensional autoencoder adapter for CSI, and explicit gradient calculations supporting CUDA implementation. Most SGD/CUDA settings move to Appendix E unchanged. However, v1's six-wavelength cube size and three-neighbor initialization details are omitted, and values for v2's new loss weights are unspecified.

R1.justification: V1 chiefly positions RFSPM against NeRF2 and NeWRF. V2 develops substantial comparisons with RF-3DGS, WRF-GS, and WRF-GS+, emphasizing its MLP-free representation and phase modeling. Added Gaussian-splatting, generalizable RF-field, and wave-expansion literature substantially revises the novelty argument.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around GSRF and new preliminaries. The standalone scalability-fidelity section disappears; much scenario, optimization, CUDA, implementation, and practical-benefit material moves into appendices. Discussion and conclusion are reorganized, and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to single-column pages with wrapped figures. V1's architecture Figure 4 becomes an adapted Figure 1 in v2. Retained plots are rearranged and expanded, the LoRa figure is removed, and CSI/BLE-timing figures plus ablation and sensitivity tables are added.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps through direct complex-CSI experiments, component ablations, and WRF-GS comparisons. These substantially strengthen evidence for the central claims, while explicit renderer and gradient documentation improves inspectability. The gains outweigh the lost LoRa application study, although undefined ± reporting, missing loss-weight settings, and inconsistent appendix equations still limit reproducibility and mathematical precision.
